write.title: How fs::write works
write.description: Creates (or overwrites) a file with the given contents, in one call.

slides.caption: Opens, writes everything, and closes the file.
The file is created or truncated.
Use OpenOptions with append(true) to add to a file instead.

read_to_string.title: How fs::read_to_string works
read_to_string.description: Reads a whole text file into a String.

slides.caption: Fails if the file is missing or not valid UTF-8.
The file is opened and read.
For huge files, read line by line with BufReader instead.

read.title: How fs::read works
read.description: Reads a whole file into a Vec<u8>.

slides.caption: No UTF-8 check: any bytes work.
The file is gone for good.
remove_dir_all deletes a whole folder tree; use it carefully.

create_dir_all.title: How fs::create_dir_all works
create_dir_all.description: Creates a folder and any missing parent folders.

slides.caption: No error if the folders already exist.
out, out/2024 and out/2024/logs are created as needed.
create_dir fails if the parent is missing.

exists.title: How fs::exists works
exists.description: Whether a path exists, as a Result.

slides.caption: Path::exists returns false on errors too; fs::exists tells you about them.
Checking first and then opening can race; often just open and handle NotFound.

metadata.title: How fs::metadata works
metadata.description: Information about a file: size, type, times.

slides.caption: metadata follows symlinks to the real file.
modified() gives the last change time.

copy.title: How fs::copy works
copy.description: Copies a file's contents to another path.

slides.caption: The target is overwritten if it exists.
The file is moved, not copied.
Moving between drives may fail: copy then remove instead.

read_dir.title: How fs::read_dir works
read_dir.description: Lists the entries of a folder.

title.text: for entry in fs::read_dir(dir)? { let entry = entry?; ... }

slides.caption: Each entry has a path(), file_name() and metadata().
Sort the names if you need a fixed order.
Subfolders are not entered; recurse yourself or use a crate like walkdir.

create.title: How File::create works
create.description: Opens a file for writing, creating it or emptying it first.

slides.caption: An existing file is emptied; use OpenOptions to append instead.
File::create_new fails if the file already exists.

open.title: How File::open works
open.description: Opens an existing file for reading.

slides.caption: It fails if the file does not exist.
The file exists: you get a File.
Wrap it in BufReader::new to read lines.

append.title: How OpenOptions::append works
append.description: Opens a file so that every write goes to the end.

slides.caption: Existing contents are kept; new data is added after them.
Add .create(true) to create the file if it is missing.

create_dir.title: How fs::create_dir works
create_dir.description: Creates one new folder; the parent must exist.

slides.caption: Refuses to delete a folder that still has contents.

remove_dir_all.title: How fs::remove_dir_all works
remove_dir_all.description: Deletes a folder and everything inside it.

slides.caption: No recycle bin: everything is deleted for good.
Double-check the path before calling it.

canonicalize.title: How fs::canonicalize works
canonicalize.description: The absolute path with . and .. resolved and symlinks followed.

slides.caption: std::path::absolute does not touch the disk.

new.title: How DirBuilder::new works
new.description: Starts configuring how folders are created.

slides.caption: A builder for create_dir with options.
On Unix you can also set the permission mode.

recursive.title: How DirBuilder::recursive works
recursive.description: Makes create() also create missing parent folders.

slides.caption: No error if the folder already exists.
Without it, a missing parent gives NotFound.

dir_builder-create.title: How DirBuilder::create works
dir_builder-create.description: Creates the folder with the builder's settings.

slides.caption: With recursive(true), an existing folder is fine.
Without recursive it would be AlreadyExists.

path.title: How DirEntry::path works
path.description: The full path of an entry found by read_dir.

file_name.title: How DirEntry::file_name works
file_name.description: Just the name of the entry, as an OsString.

file_type.title: How DirEntry::file_type works
file_type.description: Whether the entry is a file, folder or symlink.

slides.caption: Many systems report the type while listing.
Use it to recurse only into folders.

dir_entry-metadata.title: How DirEntry::metadata works
dir_entry-metadata.description: Size, type and times of an entry.

slides.caption: Saves building the path and calling fs::metadata.
Does not follow symlinks on some platforms.

len.title: How Metadata::len works
len.description: The size of the file in bytes.

slides.caption: For folders the value is system-specific.
Check sizes before reading huge files.
The opposite of is_file for normal entries.

is_symlink.title: How Metadata::is_symlink works
is_symlink.description: true for symbolic links (use symlink_metadata to see them).

slides.caption: fs::metadata follows links, so it never reports one.
Creating symlinks needs extra rights on Windows.

metadata-file_type.title: How Metadata::file_type works
metadata-file_type.description: The kind of entry: file, folder or symlink.

slides.caption: FileType has is_file, is_dir and is_symlink.
Same information as the is_* shortcuts.

modified.title: How Metadata::modified works
modified.description: When the file was last changed.

slides.caption: Build tools compare these times to decide what to rebuild.
Not every file system records it precisely.

accessed.title: How Metadata::accessed works
accessed.description: When the file was last read (if the system tracks it).

slides.caption: Many systems update it lazily or not at all.
Do not rely on it for program logic.

created.title: How Metadata::created works
created.description: When the file was created (where the system records it).

slides.caption: Windows and macOS record it; some Linux file systems do not.
A newly written file is normally writable.
On Unix, PermissionsExt gives the mode bits.

readonly.title: How Permissions::readonly works
readonly.description: true if the file cannot be written.

slides.caption: On Unix it checks the write bits for everyone.

set_readonly.title: How Permissions::set_readonly works
set_readonly.description: Changes the read-only flag on a Permissions value (apply it with set_permissions).

slides.caption: Changing the value alone does not touch the file.
The flag is set on the value.
Get the current permissions, change them, then apply.
File::set_permissions works on an open file.

file_type-is_file.title: How FileType::is_file works
file_type-is_file.description: true if the entry type is a regular file.

slides.caption: Exactly one of is_file, is_dir, is_symlink is true for normal entries.

file_type-is_dir.title: How FileType::is_dir works
file_type-is_dir.description: true if the entry type is a folder.

slides.caption: Use it to decide whether to recurse.
Pairs with read_dir for walking trees.

file_type-is_symlink.title: How FileType::is_symlink works
file_type-is_symlink.description: true if the entry type is a symbolic link.

slides.caption: Only symlink_metadata or DirEntry::file_type can report links.

symlink_metadata.title: How fs::symlink_metadata works
symlink_metadata.description: Metadata of the path itself, without following a symlink.

slides.caption: For a symlink you learn about the link; for files it equals metadata.

read_link.title: How fs::read_link works
read_link.description: The target a symbolic link points to.

slides.caption: Errors when the path is not a symlink.
The path is a plain file.
On a real symlink it returns the stored target path.

hard_link.title: How fs::hard_link works
hard_link.description: A second name for the same file data.

slides.caption: Changes through one name are visible through the other.
b.txt is created as another name.
Reading it gives the same content.
The data is freed only when every name is removed.

openoptions-new.title: How OpenOptions::new works
openoptions-new.description: Starts describing how to open a file.

slides.caption: Turn on the modes you need, then call open.

openoptions-read.title: How OpenOptions::read works
openoptions-read.description: Allows reading from the opened file.

openoptions-write.title: How OpenOptions::write works
openoptions-write.description: Allows writing; without truncate, it overwrites from the start.

slides.caption: The rest of the old content stays.
Add truncate(true) to start empty, or append(true) to add at the end.

truncate.title: How OpenOptions::truncate works
truncate.description: Empties the file when opening it.

openoptions-create.title: How OpenOptions::create works
openoptions-create.description: Creates the file if it does not exist.

slides.caption: Existing files are opened as they are.
create_new fails if it already exists.

create_new.title: How OpenOptions::create_new works
create_new.description: Creates a new file, failing if it already exists.

openoptions-open.title: How OpenOptions::open works
openoptions-open.description: Opens the file with the chosen options.

slides.caption: Without read, write or append, opening fails.
Always pick read, write or append.

file-create_new.title: How File::create_new works
file-create_new.description: Creates a new file for writing; fails if it exists.

slides.caption: Asks about the file you already have open.
Cannot be fooled by the path changing meanwhile.

set_len.title: How File::set_len works
set_len.description: Truncates or extends the file to a size.

slides.caption: Growing fills the new space with zero bytes.

sync_all.title: How File::sync_all works
sync_all.description: Waits until the file's data and metadata are really on disk.

slides.caption: Writes normally sit in OS buffers for a while.
Data is written to the OS.
sync_all flushes it to the device.
Slow: use it for important data only.

sync_data.title: How File::sync_data works
sync_data.description: Like sync_all, but may skip metadata such as times.

slides.caption: Enough when only the contents matter.
It is flushed to the device.

try_clone.title: How File::try_clone works
try_clone.description: A second handle to the same open file, sharing the position.

slides.caption: Both handles move the same read/write position.
Useful to give one handle to another thread.

file-set_permissions.title: How File::set_permissions works
file-set_permissions.description: Changes the permissions of an open file.

slides.caption: Same as fs::set_permissions, but on an open file.
Avoids races with the path being replaced.
Build tools and backups use these times.

set_times.title: How File::set_times works
set_times.description: Sets several file times at once using FileTimes.

slides.caption: Only the times you set are changed.
set_modified is the shortcut for one time.

file_times-new.title: How FileTimes::new works
file_times-new.description: An empty set of file times to apply with set_times.

slides.caption: Unset times are left unchanged when applied.

file_times-set_modified.title: How FileTimes::set_modified works
file_times-set_modified.description: Chooses the modified time in a FileTimes value.

slides.caption: Record t as the modified time.

set_accessed.title: How FileTimes::set_accessed works
set_accessed.description: Chooses the last-access time in a FileTimes value.

slides.caption: Some systems do not store access times precisely.

lock.title: How File::lock works
lock.description: Takes an exclusive lock on the file, waiting if another process holds one.

slides.caption: Other programs that also lock will wait; programs that ignore locks are not stopped.
The lock is released when the File is closed.

lock_shared.title: How File::lock_shared works
lock_shared.description: Takes a shared (read) lock: many readers, no writer.

slides.caption: An exclusive lock must wait until all shared locks are gone.

try_lock.title: How File::try_lock works
try_lock.description: Takes an exclusive lock only if it is free right now.

slides.caption: Good for "is another instance already running?".

try_lock_shared.title: How File::try_lock_shared works
try_lock_shared.description: Takes a shared lock only if no exclusive lock is held.

slides.caption: Fails at once while someone has the exclusive lock.
Release with unlock or by closing.

unlock.title: How File::unlock works
unlock.description: Releases a lock taken with lock or lock_shared.

slides.caption: Closing the file also releases it.
a holds the lock; b cannot get it.
Unlock as soon as you are done.
